projects.name: CodeBaseGPT
projects.tagline: Understand any codebase, with receipts: an interactive architecture map, and answers from the code with file-and-line citations.
projects.problem: Students and developers who are new to a codebase need to see how it fits together, and need answers they can check against the real code.
projects.built: A Next.js app that imports a repository, parses it with Tree-sitter into files, symbols, imports and calls, and shows the result in an interactive Codebase Atlas. Gemma answers questions from retrieved code, and Student Stuck Mode combines the repository with live web research to explain a problem at beginner, intermediate or advanced level.
notes: Tree-sitter parsing for TypeScript, JavaScript, Python, Java, C and C++
Hybrid retrieval: Postgres full-text search, symbol definitions and call sites, importers of the focused file, and optional pgvector embeddings
The server validates citation labels and flags any the model invented; with no matching code it says so and makes no model call
Repository evidence, web sources and the AI's reasoning are shown as three separate sections
Insights measured from the index, including import cycles (Tarjan SCC) and most-depended-on files
104 Vitest unit and integration tests, plus Playwright end-to-end tests; MIT licence
projects.limits: Graphs are capped at 400 nodes and ranked by connectivity. The complexity score is a documented heuristic, not a bug report.

media.alt: CodeBaseGPT landing page with the headline "Read any codebase like you wrote it."
media.caption: Live site — codebasegpt.vercel.app

projects.name: Hamqadam
projects.tagline: A branch-to-head-office management platform and bilingual public website for a volunteer organisation. Built for ShipLens Challenge #01.
projects.problem: Spreadsheet and WhatsApp reporting leaves a head office without approved, auditable records from its branches.
projects.built: Branch Leads record collections and submit weekly reports, the Finance Reviewer approves or returns them, HR turns volunteer applications into members, and head office sees everything on one dashboard. The public site runs in English and in right-to-left Urdu.
notes: Rules enforced in PostgreSQL: a 7-day collection lock, approved-week checks, correction limits and an append-only audit log
Role permission matrix tested for every role against every action
CSV and PDF exports scoped by role and audited
Sign-in lockout after failed attempts, a forced first-login password change, and a content security policy
CI runs unit, integration and Playwright end-to-end tests, with deploys through a Render hook
Built with Claude Code and Gemini, disclosed in the repository's AI-USAGE.md as the challenge requires
projects.limits: Runs on Render's free plan, which sleeps when idle, so the first page can take up to a minute. The data is sample data.
projects.sourceNote: The repository is named ShipLens after the challenge.

projects.name: Orbit
projects.tagline: A private academic command center for a NUST student: classes, deadlines, marks, attendance, calendar, tasks and reminders in one place.
projects.problem: Academic information is spread across the LMS, Qalam, email and calendars, and it is hard to tell which source an item came from or how fresh it is.
projects.built: A single-user Next.js app with a daily overview, per-course standing and attendance risk, a marks target planner, a timetable with conflict detection, a calendar, Markdown notes and reminders. Every item shows its source and freshness.
notes: Raw percentage, weighted contribution and official grade are kept separate
Email-derived assignments stay "Suggested" until confirmed
Moodle LMS sync or .ics upload, and CSV import for Qalam, which has no API
Argon2id, TOTP 2FA, session revocation, rate limiting and an audit log
89 Vitest unit and integration tests, plus Playwright end-to-end tests
projects.limits: Private and single-user: registration is disabled, so visitors can only see the sign-in page. LMS sync has not been tested with real student data yet.
projects.sourceNote: An independent student-built tool. Not an official NUST application, and not affiliated with NUST, its LMS or Qalam.

projects.name: DAYBREAK
projects.tagline: A personal morning newspaper: real reporting ranked around one reader, as a web paper and a matching PDF. Built for the NaSCon'26 AI Hackathon.
projects.problem: News feeds either show everyone the same front page or bury readers in an endless stream. A reader wants one finishable paper about what matters to them — with every story traceable to the original reporting.
projects.built: A Next.js 16 app on Vercel that ingests 43 RSS feeds from 21 publishers (Dawn, Business Recorder, BBC, The Guardian, Nature and more), ranks stories against each reader's sections, region and muted topics, learns from saves, skips and "not interested", and renders the saved edition as a web newspaper and a multi-page A4 PDF. Story Explorer groups the same event across newsrooms.
notes: Every story links to its publisher; only headlines and short excerpts are stored
Ranking is deterministic, with diversity rules and a "Beyond your usual" slot; learned feedback weights decay over time and can be inspected and reset
Optional AI layer: one structured call per edition, validated with Zod; summaries are rejected if they cite numbers, people or places absent from the source
Without an API key it still works and says so — the paper is labelled "No AI text in this edition"
Saved editions are immutable: Postgres triggers forbid rewrites, so the archive, web page and PDF always match
SSRF-safe feed fetching from a fixed source list; Supabase Auth with row-level security
177 Vitest tests, plus a Playwright reader journey; CI on GitHub Actions

projects.name: FinDost AI
projects.tagline: Cash-flow early warning and recovery planning for Pakistani shops, households and students — in English and Urdu.
projects.problem: A shop can be profitable on paper and still run out of cash: customers pay late (udhaar) while rent, suppliers and bills fall due on fixed dates.
projects.built: A Next.js frontend and a FastAPI backend over Supabase Postgres: a digital khata with receivables and payables, CSV import that understands Roman Urdu headers and Pakistani formats, a day-by-day 30-day cash forecast, early warnings with the records behind them, a what-if shock simulator, and recovery options priced by re-running the forecast. Built with Aiman as a contributor.
notes: Every figure comes from a deterministic engine; the forecast model is chosen per workspace by back-testing
AI is optional and opt-in (Groq / Gemini): it words answers and reads receipts into rows you review — a reply is discarded if it contains a number not in the evidence
Workspaces with owner / editor / viewer roles; a workspace id from the browser is honoured only for its members, tested for tenant isolation
Enterprise flow: proposed actions → owner approval → completion, with an audit trail
171 backend pytest tests, with AI providers mocked

media.alt: FinDost AI command center showing a projected cash shortage warning, balances, receivables, bills due and forecasts
media.caption: Shop dashboard with fictional demo data

projects.name: ShopFlow
projects.tagline: Marketplace and shop-management platform for small independent sellers, with an AI-assisted customer inbox.
projects.problem: Small sellers — Instagram and WhatsApp shops, boutiques — juggle stock, orders, a store page and customer messages across separate tools.
projects.built: A multi-tenant Next.js + Django REST platform: per-shop inventory with variants, orders, a public storefront with cart and checkout, customer records, analytics, and **ReplyFlow** — an inbox where Claude drafts replies grounded in the shop's live catalogue and the customer's orders, which a person reviews before sending.
notes: JWT auth with 15-minute access tokens, refresh rotation and blacklisting; tokens live in httpOnly cookies behind a Next.js proxy
Owner / admin / staff roles enforced by DRF permission classes, with tenant-isolation tests
AI drafts use live prices and stock, are told to ignore instructions inside customer messages, and are never auto-sent
Stripe behind a payment-provider interface with signature-verified webhooks; live stores currently use cash on delivery
Per-endpoint rate limits (auth, AI, checkout, password reset), HSTS and secure cookies in production
~126 backend tests + Vitest; CI runs lint, type-check, tests, build and `npm audit`
projects.extra: Also shipped a Kotlin Android wrapper (signed v1.0.1 APK) with persistent sessions, camera uploads and external-link routing.
projects.sourceNote: Source is private — happy to walk through the code.

projects.name: PharmaPro
projects.tagline: Offline desktop pharmacy system: batch and expiry tracking, point of sale, receipts and profit reports.
projects.problem: A small pharmacy has to sell from the right batch, never sell expired stock, and keep working when the internet doesn't.
projects.built: A PySide6 (Qt) desktop app over SQLAlchemy + SQLite with a medicine catalogue, batch-based stock receiving, a barcode-friendly POS with printable receipts, expenses, profit reports, charts and backup/restore — packaged as a Windows `.exe` and a Debian `.deb`.
notes: First-expiry-first-out batch allocation at checkout; expired batches are blocked from sale
Database CHECK constraints make negative stock impossible; writes run in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transactions
UI talks only to a service layer, so business rules are tested without opening a window
Fully offline — a test asserts the app makes no network calls
81 pytest tests including offscreen UI smoke tests; CI builds the installers
projects.sourceNote: v1.0.0 builds for Windows and Linux.

projects.name: Library Management System
projects.tagline: Desktop library software in C++17 with a Qt 6 interface and role-based workflows.
projects.problem: Students, faculty and admins need different powers over the same catalogue, loans and members — and the data must survive restarts without a database.
projects.built: Students borrow and return their own books; faculty manage the catalogue and issue/return for students; the admin manages members and reviews volunteer applications. Everything persists to CSV through a hand-written parser and file handler.
notes: Model, storage and rules are plain C++ with no Qt — the GUI only calls into `Library`
Permissions resolved through virtual functions on `Person` subclasses — no role checks in the GUI
Loan rules: 14-day loans, 5-book cap, fee/warning blocks, late returns add a warning
Atomic saves: each CSV is written to `.tmp` then renamed, so a crash never leaves half a file
CSV parser handles quoted commas and escaped quotes; templated `loadTable<T>` / `saveTable<T>`
68 / 68 core checks pass with a single `g++` command
projects.limits: Passwords are stored in plain text — acceptable for a class project, and documented in the README.

projects.name: Air Draw Controller
projects.tagline: Computer-vision interface: draw in the air with your index finger using webcam hand tracking.
projects.problem: Can an ordinary webcam become a touch-free drawing surface, in real time, without extra hardware?
projects.built: A real-time loop: mirrored OpenCV capture → MediaPipe Hands landmarks → a finger-state gesture check → strokes on a canvas overlaid on the live video.
notes: Gesture detection from landmark geometry: a finger is "up" when its tip is above its middle joint
Draws only in the "index up, others down" pose; any other pose lifts the pen, so no stray lines
Canvas merged onto each frame with a NumPy mask; [[c]] clears, [[q]] quits
projects.sourceNote: Single-file prototype — source not published yet.

principles.title: Keep the logic out of the UI
principles.body: The Library System's rules are plain C++ and PharmaPro's live in a service layer — both are tested without opening a window.

principles.title: Make bad states impossible
principles.body: Database constraints stop negative stock; a `Date` can't hold 30 February; saves are atomic.

principles.title: AI drafts, people decide
principles.body: ShopFlow's assistant is grounded in real shop data, won't invent prices, and never sends without a human.

principles.title: Tests before claims
principles.body: Every number on this site comes from a test suite, the source, or a live deployment.
